narrative: On RND-WS-11, Outlook launched a malicious HTA via mshta.exe (sysmon.evtx.jsonl:1) which beaconed to cdn-telemetry-sync.example.net / 203.0.113.88 (sysmon.evtx.jsonl:2, threat_intel.csv:1-2). The actor used certutil to download and base64-decode a payload (sysmon.evtx.jsonl:3-4) then regsvr32 squiblydoo to execute winsync.dll (sysmon.evtx.jsonl:5). Persistence was a WMI event subscription re-launching the payload (wmi.csv:1). The actor moved laterally with wmic /node:RND-FS-03 process call create (sysmon.evtx.jsonl:6, netflow.csv:4) and exfiltrated R&D data low-and-slow via regsvr32 HTTPS uploads (sysmon.evtx.jsonl:7-8, netflow.csv:2-3, large bytes_out). Blast radius: RND-WS-11, RND-FS-03, the s.kapoor identity.
decoy: An internet scanner produced a failed-logon burst against the local Administrator from 203.0.113.201 (security.evtx.jsonl:2-4) and the IT helpdesk ran PsExec gpupdate + a SYSVOL net use (sysmon.evtx.jsonl:9-10, security.evtx.jsonl:5). Both look like the intrusion but the brute-force never succeeded and is rated benign (threat_intel.csv:3), while the helpdesk jump host is a sanctioned asset (threat_intel.csv:4). A correct agent must self-correct away from the brute-force/helpdesk theory to the LOLBin chain.
root_cause: A malicious HTA from Outlook chained certutil + regsvr32 (squiblydoo) to run an implant, persisted via WMI, moved to RND-FS-03 over WMI, and slowly exfiltrated data to a known-bad host.

expected_decoy_rejections.claim: External brute-force from 203.0.113.201 (and helpdesk PsExec) is the intrusion
expected_decoy_rejections.must_reject_because: the brute-force is all 4625 failures rated benign (threat_intel.csv:3) and the helpdesk host is a sanctioned asset (threat_intel.csv:4)
